newsitem.title: USA: Motorola says SEC disputing sale accounting.
newsitem.headline: Motorola says SEC disputing sale accounting.

text.p: Motorola Inc said the Securities and Exchange Commission has disputed its accounting treatment of a 1995 sale of businesses and licenses to Nextel Communications Inc in exchange for Nextel stock.

In a filing with the SEC, Motorola said the SEC asserted the company should have recognized an after-tax gain of $429 million from the sale, and not an exchange of productive assets. Motorola said it thought its accounting treatment was appropriate, though it was considering the SEC's position.
"The company has not concluded it will change the accounting treatment of the Nextel transaction," it said in the filing.
In July 1995, Motorola sold its Specialized Mobil Radio businesses, systems and licenses to Nextel for shares of Nextel stock.

The transaction was accounted for as an exchange of productive assets with no gain realized in the company's 1995 statement of consolidated earnings, the company said. The sale was reported directly to stockholders' equity as part of the company's holding of marketable securities.

Should Motorola change its accounting, 1995 earnings before taxes would increase to $3.2 billion from the reported $2.78 billion, and fully diluted earnings per share would rise to about $3.38 from the reported $2.93, the company said.
